rows.en: Lodis: "It seems you rescued her safely."
Ymir: "Yes. How did things go on your end?"
Lodis: "They said it was outrageous to use Liebhofen
without permission, and so on.
Since when did Liebhofen become
their property?"
Forzen: "Politicians have always been the sort
who only see things
in whatever way suits them.
Anyway, we managed to quiet them down,
and Kasumi is safe. All's well that ends well."
Touya: "What's so well about it?!
If you'd done your job properly,
none of this would've happened!"
Forzen: "Ah, I'm ashamed of myself.
Well, let's put the past behind us
and think about what comes next."
Touya: "You know..."
Kasumi: "Touya-chan, it isn't Forzen's fault.
He helped me when I felt like
I'd be crushed by anxiety."
Touya: "W-Well, yeah, but..."
Kasumi: "And I got to see you again, Touya-chan.
I think things worked out for the best."
Lodis: "I'm glad you're such a kindhearted woman.
I hope you never lose that kindness..."
Kasumi: "Huh? Y-Yes..."
Lodis: "I see. You're confused.
Don't worry. We'll take responsibility
for providing for you here. You needn't be afraid."
Kasumi: "U-Um..."
Fain: "Y-Y-Your Highness?!"
Celica: "All right, that's enough. Brother, I know you're trying to reassure her,
but didn't I tell you to stop casually taking a girl's hands
and gazing into her eyes?
That's why you're always getting into trouble.
...And don't you feel a sharp stare on the back of your neck?"
Sisk: "..."
Lodis: "W-Well, there's Kasumi to consider,
and I need to hear your report.
Shall we go to Lady Ivel's room?"
Kasumi: "Um..."
Lodis: "What is it?"
Kasumi: "I'd like to help
all of you..."
Ymir: "Do you mean
you want to fight alongside us?"
Kasumi: "Yes. Apparently I have the aptitude to pilot those robots,
and I've heard you're short of people.
I can't just ignore people in trouble.
If there's anything I can do to help,
please let me."
Kasumi: "...And I've finally found you, Touya-chan.
I don't want to be separated again..."
Lodis: "I see... In that case,
we'd be grateful. But are you really sure?"
Kasumi: "Yes."
Aurelie: "I don't like it.
I don't want you taking that naive idea of staying close to the man you like
into a Spirit Mech."
Ymir: "Aurelie?!"
Aurelie: "We aren't professional soldiers ourselves.
And the fighting will only get tougher.
Someone driven by nothing but flighty feelings
could put everyone around her in danger.
To be blunt, you'd be a liability."
Defend Kasumi
Stay Silent
Touya: "I get what you're saying,
but don't put it like that."
Kasumi: "Touya-chan..."
Aurelie: "...This isn't a game. It's real combat.
And can you really fight?
You might have to kill someone!"
Kasumi: "Well..."
Aurelie: "Get into a Spirit Mech thinking like that,
and you'll be the one who dies!"
Kasumi: "..."
Clovis: "Aurelie..."
Aurelie: "Wh-What?"
Clovis: "You're kind.
You think Kasumi won't be able to bear fighting, don't you?"
Aurelie: "..."
Clovis: "Like you just said,
this isn't a game. It's a battle.
Sooner or later, she'll take a life with her own hands.
The guilt might crush her
when that happens... Just like it did you once."
Touya: "That happened...?"
Aurelie: "...It was a long time ago."
Kasumi: "I..."
Aurelie: "...Sigh. Don't look at me like that.
You're making me look like a bully."
Kasumi: "I-I'm sorry..."
Aurelie: "...Do what you want.
But I warned you."
Kasumi: "Aurelie..."
Touya: "Don't look like that."
Kasumi: "Touya-chan, is it okay for me to stay here?
Am I just causing everyone trouble...?"
Touya: "What are you talking about? Of course not.
It's okay. Don't worry.
...Or do you not want to be here?"
Kasumi: "No! That's not it."
Touya: "Then don't worry about it.
And if it comes to it, I'll protect you."
Kasumi: "...Okay. I believe you."
Kasumi: "B-But..."
Fain: "That's not true! Look into her eyes!
No one with eyes like that would ever lie!
Even if God permitted such a thing,
I, Fain Jin Barion, would not!!"
Aurelie: "No, I never said she was lying..."
Fain: "Besides, if she's in danger...
I-I'll... I'll..."
Clovis: "Oh? You'll protect her?
You really have... fallen for her, haven't you?"
Fain: "What?! Wh-Wh-What are you talking about?!"
Aurelie: "...This isn't a game. It's real combat.
And can you really fight?
You might have to kill someone!"
Kasumi: "Well..."
Aurelie: "Get into a Spirit Mech thinking like that,
and you'll be the one who dies!"
Kasumi: "..."
Clovis: "Aurelie..."
Aurelie: "Wh-What?"
Clovis: "You're kind.
You think Kasumi won't be able to bear fighting, don't you?"
Aurelie: "..."
Clovis: "Like you just said,
this isn't a game. It's a battle.
Sooner or later, she'll take a life with her own hands.
The guilt might crush her
when that happens... Just like it did you once."
Touya: "That happened...?"
Aurelie: "...It was a long time ago."
Kasumi: "I..."
Aurelie: "...Sigh. Don't look at me like that.
You're making me look like a bully."
Kasumi: "I-I'm sorry..."
Aurelie: "...Well, it's your decision.
Do what you want. But I warned you."
Kasumi: "Aurelie..."
Fain: "Don't worry! I'll protect you!"
Kasumi: "Huh? Y-Yeah... Thank you..."
Lodis: "Well, Kasumi can come with us as a pilot candidate.
She needs to take an aptitude test,
after all. Is that all right?"
Kasumi: "Y-Yes. Thank you."
Forzen: "Oh, who is that gentleman?"
Ymir: "Oh, that's right.
Let me introduce the man who protected Kasumi.
This is Bernst Bulow."
Bernst: "A pleasure to meet you.
I haven't done anything so remarkable."
Lodis: "My apologies for not introducing myself.
I'm Lodis Lang Mestina."
Bernst: "Meeting the Crown Prince of Agarthia
is a great honor."
Celica: "Brother, he did something else important for us.
He got us parts from Zigrim's Armored Mechs.
Their new models, at that."
Lodis: "Oh...?"
Celica: "And the results of my analysis honestly
surprised me. The technology is related to Spirit Mechs... No,
more specifically, it's in the same line as Rayblade's
technology.
But it's only a shoddy imitation. What a sloppy
job."
Touya: "You can tell all that from such tiny parts?"
Celica: "The wiring has no 'flair.'
I think they put it together on a superficial understanding,
without really knowing what they were doing."
Bernst: "I see. 'Flair.' That's quite an interesting
way to put it."
Ymir: "But that doesn't establish that ≪Ze=Ode≫
is involved, does it?"
Bernst: "Not necessarily. Wouldn't you agree?"
Celica: "Yes. Rayblade is a product of technology
far beyond our own capabilities.
If that's being used, someone who can analyze Rayblade
or another mech of comparable ability
must be helping them.
It's hard to imagine they got information from Rayblade,
which was completely sealed until recently.
That leaves only one answer..."
Clovis: "≪Ze=Ode≫... Huh."
Celica: "Exactly. The Spirit Mech data was completely secure too.
Unless someone analyzed Rayblade before I did
and stole that data."
Lodis: "...But why use Zigrim?
And why provide technology and have them build
Armored Mechs, rather than helping them directly...?"
Bernst: "...Probably because of 'Goderius.'
Its appearance hasn't been confirmed yet, has it?"
Ymir: "N-No... But how did you know that?"
Bernst: "That news report caught my interest,
so I did some investigating.
I do have friends who are well informed."
Lodis: "I see. We're about to meet with Matriarch Ivel
to discuss what comes next.
Would you join us?"
Bernst: "...Is it all right for an outsider like me to attend?"
Lodis: "If you'll tell us
what you know."
Bernst: "You think I know information
valuable enough to warrant that?"
Lodis: "I hope so."
Bernst: "...Heh. You really are
a skilled negotiator, Crown Prince Lodis.
Very well.
I'll tell you everything I know."
Growster: "Come in."
Lyle: "Hey."
Growster: "What do you want? I'm busy."
Lyle: "Are you really going to invade Agarthia?"
Growster: "We can leave York to Grad."
Lyle: "The queen's death has been officially announced too.
But I hear York's knights are still alive.
Isn't it dangerous to leave them loose?"
Growster: "Now is our chance to crush our old enemy, Agarthia!
York can be dealt with easily enough."
Lyle: "I heard Agarthia is developing
new models too."
Growster: "They may think they've hidden it,
but it's futile before Zigrim's proud intelligence service.
They should stick to hiding their heads."
Lyle: "...Do you have a personal grudge against Agarthia's Revios
or something?"
Growster: "Hmph! That's none of your business.
More importantly, Agarthia's new models
have specifications we can't ignore.
We must settle this before they're deployed
to the front in earnest..."
Lyle: "So you can make a coolheaded judgment about that."
Growster: "Are you mocking me?
Anyone who can't assess the enemy's strength correctly
isn't fit to be a general."
Lyle: "Sorry about that.
...So what reason will you use to declare war?"
Growster: "The biological weapons sighted in York.
Those are Agarthian weapons, and York is our territory.
That makes it a territorial violation.
...A sufficient pretext, wouldn't you say?"
Lyle: "You're practically just picking a fight..."
Growster: "That's what war is. We'll take the royal capital in one strike
and show them Zigrim's might!"
Lyle: "I see. A lightning campaign...
Well, that poses no problem for us either."
Growster: "What problem could there possibly be?
Just stay here and watch our army win."
Lyle: "I'll do that for now..."
Growster: "And that man is relaxing at his villa
at a time like this... What does he think he's doing
as head of state?!"
Lyle: (Tch. Here comes the griping again...)
Growster: "Making a man who only entered politics through
his parents' influence president and head of state
was a grave mistake to begin with. Welfare, charity...
All he does is court the public's favor.
And what did he do once he was elected?
The first thing was build that villa!
Whatever he calls it, he's just spending public money
however he pleases! Campaign promises become empty promises,
and he barely makes a token effort to fulfill them.
It's always been like that, but he's especially bad.
Compared with him, even the useless fools before him
were far better.
He's the only one who takes naps in his office!
Politicians care only about their own profit,
colluding with contractors and steeped in corruption.
The president brazenly squanders public money on himself.
What will become of this country?!
Don't you agree?! Well?!"
Lyle: "...Y-Yeah. I agree..."
Growster: "No, you still don't understand.
Fine. Today I'll explain it to you properly.
You're a lucky man, you know.
Come on, sit there."
Growster: "Now, where was I?
Oh, yes. We were discussing this country's future.
To begin with..."
Cain: "You're taking it easy when war's about to begin."
Horem: "I'm not interested.
It's merely a matter of sooner or later.
Let's prepare to transfer the data instead."
Cain: "...If he knew this project had resumed,
what would General Growster think?"
Horem: "Heh heh... By the time he notices,
he'll be my puppet too."
Cain: "...You're a frightening man."
Horem: "Am I? I'm simply honest with myself.
I thought you were too."
Cain: "Well, I suppose we're alike in that respect.
Things should get interesting now.
York fell surprisingly easily."
Horem: "The Armored Mechs Growster is so proud of
must have performed well. Personally, I regret that
we couldn't use the summoning device.
Who'd have thought it was linked to the Holy Land...?
We failed to obtain a Spirit Mech too.
Still, we did get data and resources.
Let's be satisfied with that."
Cain: "Then is 'she' next?"
Horem: "Yes."
Cain: "In that case, I should have brought her back then."
Horem: "Using force is inelegant.
We should respect her wishes as much as possible."
Cain: "A project to take away people's wills on one hand,
and respect for an individual's will on the other... What a contradiction."
Horem: "Isn't that what being 'human' means?"
Cain: "Heh heh heh...
Well, I'll go and do my part."
Horem: "Now, I think I'll take
a little nap..."
Ivel: "...I see. So the invasion of York was ordered
by President Horem, rather than ≪Ze=Ode≫...
Is that what you're saying?"
Bernst: "Unless ≪Ze=Ode≫ was behind the president himself.
That would be another matter."
Lodis: "A military action of that scale
must have had the president's approval
as head of state. I'd assumed as much...
But the current president was rumored to be a puppet
who merely approved parliament's decisions..."
Celica: "They call him a 'daytime lantern,' don't they?"
Touya: "Huh. They have that expression in this world too."
Celica: "Sure. But if he's suddenly started taking action,
couldn't that mean the president himself is being controlled?"
Xiujian: "That's unlikely.
Rather than use someone dismissed as a puppet,
it would be surer to win over someone
with greater influence.
A major military figure, for example."
Lodis: "...General Growster.
He certainly fits the conditions.
You could say he rules the military as a dictator."
Bernst: "With not all of ≪Ze=Ode≫ assembled yet,
they're probably waiting for its revival,
or acting to bring it about.
Shouldn't we work on countermeasures in the meantime?"
Touya: "What happens when all of ≪Ze=Ode≫ is together?"
Ymir: "Probably the same phenomenon as the ≪Terror of Ze=Ode≫
would occur."
Bernst: "Or they might be able to cause it deliberately."
Touya: "Hey, isn't that really bad?"
Bernst: "Yes. That's why we should devise
every countermeasure we can in the meantime."
Celica: "Right. We're close to understanding ≪Ze=Ode≫'s field,
so if we build a device
and fit it to the Spirit Mechs, we might manage...
Though it's a brute-force 'countermeasure.'"
Clovis: "Anyway, we still don't have enough information.
All we can do is watch Zigrim's movements."
Ivel: "Yes. And your own problems
are beginning to surface now."
Touya: "What do you mean?"
Ivel: "The Spirit Mechs.
Agarthia's government has claimed ownership
of them.
They say that, since the eldest princess, Celica, designed the Spirit Mechs,
Agarthia has a right to own them too.
They want us to hand over the mechs that currently have pilots,
or make Liebhofen and its crew an Agarthian organization.
That's what they've demanded.
If things continue like this, they'll find some pretext
to detain you. That's plain to see.
Chairman Rakbal is appealing to parliament on our behalf,
but it will only buy us time."
Touya: "Who do they think they are...?!"
Clovis: "That's all governments amount to, in the end."
Lodis: "It's truly shameful.
To claim rights over you only now..."
Celica: "Why don't we just ignore them?"
Ivel: "That will probably be the result.
Liebhofen was built as the Spirit Mechs' mothership
and your base of operations in the first place.
Now that ≪Ze=Ode≫'s revival is certain,
we need to watch developments everywhere."
Lodis: "As of today, we establish a group to investigate ≪Ze=Ode≫,
a research organization.
Its base will be Liebhofen. Its members, of course, are you."
Arthur: "So we make the first move
before they can lay a hand on us..."
Lodis: "Unfortunately, Agarthia as it is now
lacks the capacity to accept you,
and this is beyond what I can resolve by myself."
Ivel: "They'll complain again,
but the rights they claim
never existed in the first place.
There are any number of ways out.
And since that recent news report, distrust of the government
has turned to criticism. Facing ≪Ze=Ode≫ head-on,
the Spirit Mechs are where the public's hopes
now lie.
The government merely wants to exploit that.
We need only turn that to our advantage."
Ymir: "Lady Ivel, in that case, I'll stay with you..."
Ivel: "No. You must see
the truth with your own eyes."
Ymir: "The truth...?"
Ivel: "Yes. What ≪Ze=Ode≫ really is,
and what they're trying to do.
I want you to witness that in my place."
Ymir: "Lady Ivel..."
Ivel: "And you can make the Council
recognize you as my representative.
To help us negotiate from a stronger position,
I want you to remain with Liebhofen."
Ymir: "...Understood.
I humbly accept."
Garyud: "Excuse me."
Ivel: "...So you are going?"
Garyud: "Yes. To liberate York, we're heading
to Krondem.
We'll regroup there and ready ourselves for battle."
Lodis: "Our country ought to be helping you,
but..."
Garyud: "Don't let it trouble you.
Your goodwill is our greatest source of strength."
Reduce: "Hmm?"
Bernst: "..."
Garyud: "What is it?"
Reduce: "Nothing... Forgive me, but who is that gentleman?"
Bernst: "My name is Bernst Bulow.
Circumstances have brought me here to join this meeting."
Reduce: "...Aren't you a pilot?"
Bernst: "...I'm merely a researcher.
Nothing more, nothing less."
Reduce: "I see. Then I must have been mistaken.
My apologies."
Bernst: "...Not at all."
Ciel: "Father, it's about time..."
Garyud: "Yes, you're right.
Well, we'll take our leave..."
Lodis: "Wait a moment.
I think it would be best for Liebhofen and the Spirit Mechs
to accompany you and help liberate York.
What do you think?"
Celica: "Huh?!"
Ymir: "Your Highness. But that would..."
Lodis: "I understand.
I'd be recommending that you take one country's side
and be used as weapons.
But unfortunately, Agarthia as it stands
lacks the capacity to accept Liebhofen,
and I can't solve that with my personal influence.
Perhaps, as Lady Ivel suggested, a research organization
acting independently is the best approach.
But our strongest lead on ≪Ze=Ode≫ is Zigrim.
And their actions are clearly an invasion. This has already become
an issue that goes beyond national borders.
I can't believe fighting it would betray Queen Alforina
or the people who helped us.
It surely wouldn't be the wrong choice."
Fain: "I agree with His Highness!
Power itself isn't what matters. It's how we use it.
Our goal is to prevent the tragedy of 109 years ago from happening again.
Should we worry about a little temporary slander
in the pursuit of that goal?
What must we do?
We ourselves know the answer best.
Liberating York is not a battle against Zigrim.
It's a battle to put Zigrim back on the right path and draw ≪Ze=Ode≫
out into the open!"
Ai: "Wow... That's a sensible opinion, coming from you.
For once, I agree with Fain."
Celica: "It's true we don't have time.
We can't afford to leave Zigrim alone
when it's our most reliable lead..."
Arthur: "I agree. If we leave Zigrim unchecked,
they'll launch their next invasion
before long.
That will only mean more pointless fighting."
Clovis: "I'm against it, whatever the reason.
If we throw ourselves into war, the Spirit Mechs'
very existence will be called into question.
We aren't here to wage war.
We mustn't forget that."
Aurelie: "I'm against it too.
Spirit Mechs are weapons. We'll end up fighting eventually,
but there's a world of difference between responding and starting it."
Xiujian: "...Agreed."
Kasumi: "...I-I don't really understand it all,
but I think war is wrong."
Captain Roa: "Hmm."
Ymir: "Huh? Captain, do you mean..."
Captain Roa: "Hmm."
Ymir: "...No, I understand. I think he'll choose
the right path too.
...Touya. What do you think?"
Touya: "Huh? Me?"
Act as a Research Organization
Join the Liberation of York
Ymir: "...Understood. I'll announce the decision of Liebhofen's commander,
Admiral Roa Jin Krankheit.
We will act as a research organization, as Lady Ivel
has proposed.
...Your Highness, Lord Garyud, I'm sorry."
Lodis: "No, perhaps that is the right decision.
Whichever course you choose, your goal remains the same."
Garyud: "Indeed. We'll strive to liberate our country
as soon as possible so we can help investigate ≪Ze=Ode≫.
We'll do everything we can."
Fain: "...It's unfortunate, but I won't oppose the decision."
Arthur: "It can't be helped. Ai, let's accept it."
Ai: "...I know."
Celica: "Principles over efficiency...
Well, fine."
Garyud: "Then we'll take our leave.
I hope things have improved by the next time we meet."
Ciel: "Goodbye, then."
Reduce: "Excuse us."
Bernst: "Well, I can't stay too long either.
I should be going now."
Touya: "Stay too long? You only just made a bargain
so you could come with us..."
Bernst: "Oh, did I?
My memory's been terrible lately.
I've told you what I needed to. I'll be off."
Lodis: "Where will you go now?"
Bernst: "Who knows? Wherever I feel like going...
Let's leave it at that."
Lodis: "I suspect we'll meet again."
Bernst: "Yes. In the not-too-distant future.
Goodbye."
Celica: "Brother... What do you mean?"
Lodis: "Could he be... No, never mind.
Let's hope I'm imagining things."
Ivel: "It's unusual for you to say something like that."
Lodis: "Please don't tease me.
In any case, you should leave as soon as possible.
I'm sorry to rush everyone."
Ymir: "Understood. We'll depart
as soon as preparations are complete."
Ivel: "Take care.
You are yourself. Keep your heart strong."
Ymir: "...? Yes. Understood."
Celica: "Now, then..."
Lodis: "Celica, where are you going?"
Celica: "Huh? No, n-nowhere..."
Lodis: "...Don't go with them.
Father told me
to bring you back."
Celica: "Yeees."
Revios: "Too late... Trying to obtain the Spirit Mechs
only now, when the public has placed its hopes in them...
They don't need a patron anymore. Far too late..."
Geel: "Excuse me.
A report has arrived that Liebhofen is on the move.
They apparently intend to reject parliament's proposal."
Revios: "Heh heh. So that's their answer.
His Highness is being quite bold..."
Geel: "We can detain them now..."
Revios: "There's no need. Certainly, bringing them into
Agarthia now might win public opinion over to our side.
But the credit would go to them, not us.
If we keep relying on people from another world,
nothing will change. We must uphold our country's prestige
with our own hands."
Geel: "But they're an ideal force to make use of..."
Revios: "Certainly, power depends on how it's used. But now isn't the time.
To tame a wild beast, you don't pull its fangs.
You weaken it and make it submit.
The greater people's expectations,
the harsher the backlash when they're betrayed.
We'd do better to wait until then."
Geel: "Yes, sir. It wasn't my place
to offer an opinion.
...As for the reply from Zigrim,
it's just as we expected.
War seems unavoidable if this continues."
Revios: "No doubt. People who only know how to flaunt our country's prestige
could never negotiate successfully.
Events don't follow a textbook."
Geel: "Surely if you became our leader, Excellency..."
Revios: "...Colonel. We soldiers have a duty to obey
and carry out the government's decisions.
An army that acts for its own convenience is no better than bandits."
Geel: "But..."
Revios: "I don't object to the nation's system of government.
I simply can't stand the stupidity of the people who make it up.
I have no intention of becoming a politician, nor do I think I could.
It wouldn't suit me, for a start."
Geel: "..."
Revios: "Colonel. I'm proud to be a soldier.
I thought you felt the same."
Geel: "...I overstepped."
Revios: "Hmm. ...Speaking of which, how is that matter progressing?"
Geel: "Without a hitch. We're currently
testing the prototype. For mass production, though,
Renbardon seems better suited."
Revios: "I see. Then proceed that way, quickly."
Geel: "Yes, sir."
Revios: "...One more thing, Colonel.
I'd like you to refrain from acting on your own."
Geel: "What are you referring to?"
Revios: "Would Dr. Berol's laboratory mean anything to you?
Security that can be breached by such a lousy hacker is a problem,
but hiring someone like that is an even bigger one."
Geel: "...Yes, sir."
Touya: "Phew. Is that everything? ...Hmm?"
Yamato: "Come on, don't stop working... What's wrong?"
Touya: "Isn't that... Rayblade?"
Yamato: "You're right. We're taking Rayblade too..."
Ymir: "Yes."
Touya: "Oh, Ymir."
Ymir: "Leaving it here would be more dangerous,
so Lady Ivel told us to take it."
Yamato: "True. Once the Spirit Mechs are gone,
they might try to get hold of Rayblade."
Ymir: "Yes. Though Rayblade still isn't completely
repaired, so we can't use it."
Touya: "I see. After all that...? That scent..."
Ymir: "Oh, this? Lady Ivel gave it to me.
It smells nice, doesn't it?"
Touya: "...It's the same scent as back then..."
Ymir: "Is something wrong?"
Touya: "Oh, no..."
Ymir: "Really?
Well, let's head to the bridge."
Touya: "Y-Yeah..."
Maki: "No one's around, right?"
Reisuke: "Beep-beep-beep-beep."
Maki: "Good! Now!"
Maki: "Infiltration successful! Heh heh... The next Roguewar Prize
is mine. Just watch... I'll uncover Rayblade's
true identity..."
Kasumi: "So this is a Spirit Mech...
It's huge when you see it like this...
What is this feeling...?"
Ai: "I hear it's called Orbest."
Kasumi: "A-Ai... san."
Ai: "Just Ai is fine. We're going to be teammates,
so we should break down these 'walls' right at the start.
Otherwise, they'll drag on forever.
Besides, I don't like formal speech."
Kasumi: "W-Why... is that?"
Ai: "See? That. It feels so distant, doesn't it?
I think it's enough to respect someone,
even if you don't show it through words.
You don't have to get hung up on formalities.
What matters is how you feel, right?"
Kasumi: "You're amazing, Ai-san."
Ai: "Ai."
Kasumi: "Ai... chan."
Ai: "Sigh... Well, fine.
From today on, it's 'Ai-chan.' Settled.
And I'm younger than you,
so you don't have to speak so formally.
